title: Figures and axes
summary: A figure is the whole chart image. An Axes object is an area inside it where data is drawn.
introduction: A figure is the whole chart image. An Axes object is an area inside it where data is drawn. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A figure is the whole chart image. An Axes object is an area inside it where data is drawn.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Examples need Python and Matplotlib. Run them in a local notebook or suitable Python environment. Charts are described here; the website playground does not run Python.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Matplotlib. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 3])
plt.show()
blocks.title: Figures and axes

blocks.text: The line passes through the three given points. fig refers to the image; ax refers to its plotting area.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Draw the three points on paper first.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Matplotlib uses Axes as an object name; it is different from one single x or y axis.
For more detail later, use this [Matplotlib further reading](https://matplotlib.org/stable/users/explain/quick_start.html).
